_note: H9(a) check: Sun/Earth angles the site shows (frozen hourly table + the same interpolation code as the page, src/ephem.js) against JPL Horizons asked directly for the same site and minute. Times are drawn at random (fixed seed) inside the table range and never on a table row.

engine._note: H9(a) for own coordinates (item b): angles computed in the browser (src/moonsky.js through scripts/engine_angles.mjs, same grid, rounding and interpolation as the page) against JPL Horizons. Pairs = the listed-site pairs above (Horizons values reused) + pairs_per_point new pairs at each unnamed check point below (not landing sites; spread over near side, far side, limbs and both poles).

scale._note: Check at scale (ADR 0108, scripts/validate.py --scale): pairs_per_site random minutes (fixed seed, never on a table hour) at EVERY listed site of config/sites.json, from..to, which spans the frozen JPL Horizons tables and the later dates the in-browser engine computes. "Shown" = what the page shows at that minute: the frozen table read by src/ephem.js up to the table end, the engine (src/moonsky.js) after it (the rule of src/years.js sourceAt). Horizons is asked for the same minutes in batches (TLIST: one request per site and body, at most batch_max_times minutes each), at most one request every min_interval_seconds, retried up to retries times after retry_wait_seconds (times the attempt number). Every raw Horizons answer is kept in cache_file (keyed by its request URL), so a second run makes no request.
